PADA menjalankan kuasa yang diberi kan oleh sekysen 16 dan 29 Akta Lembaga
Pelabuhan 1963 [ Akta 488], Lembaga Pelabuhan Kelang , dengan kelulusan Menteri,
membuat undang-undang kecil yang berikut:

BAHAGIAN I
PERMULAAN

Nama dan permulaan kuat kuasa
1.     (1)   Undang-undang kecil ini bolehlah dinamakan Undang-Undang Kecil
Lembaga Pelabuhan Kelang (Skala Kadar, Dius dan Caj) 2012.

(2)         Undang-Undang Kecil ini mula berkuat kuasa pada 1 Julai 2012.

Tafsiran
2. Dalam Undang-Undang Kecil ini, melainkan jika konteksnya menghendaki makna
yang lain—

 "barang berbahaya " ertinya barang berbahaya sama ada dalam bentuk
bungkusan, berkontena atau diangkut secara pukal, dan termasuk barang yang
diklasifikasikan oleh Lembaga ke dalam kumpulan yang dinyatakan dalam Undang -
Undang Kecil Lembaga Pelabuhan Kelang 1965 [ L.N. 127/1965 ] dan menepati Kod
BBMA dan penyiaran PMA lain yang berkaitan yang dipinda dari semasa ke semasa dan
diguna pakai oleh Lembaga;

"bungkusan" termasuklah apa-apa kotak, bakul, tong, bekas, peti, guni, beg,
pembalut, sampul atau penutup atau benda lain yang dalamnya apa-apa kargo
ditempatkan bagi maksud untuk dibawa, dikonsain, diangkut, diimport atau dieksport;

"daerah permaliman" ertinya suatu kawasan yang diisytihar kan oleh Lembaga
di bawah seksyen 29A Akta Lembaga Pelabuhan 1963;

"dermaga" termasuklah mana -mana dindi ng dan bangunan yang bersambung
dengan persisir depan, dasar laut atau dasar sungai;

"dermaga Lembaga" ertinya dermaga yang dimiliki, di kawal atau dikendali kan
oleh Lembaga;

 "ditinggalkan kapal" berhubung dengan suatu kargo atau kontena, ertinya tidak
dibawa dalam pelayaran kapal yang diniatkan bagi kargo atau kontena itu;

 "hari" berhubung dengan  suatu transaksi, ertinya tempoh  selama dua puluh
empat jam dari masa permulaan transaksi itu;

" kapal dagang asing" ertinya kapal selain kapal dagang dalam negeri;

"kapal dagang dalam negeri" ertinya mana-mana kapal yang didafta rkan di
Malaysia yang terlibat dalam perdagangan dalam negeri sahaja;

"kargo" hendaklah termasuk ternakan, galian, barang -barang dan dagangan dari
apa jua perihalan sama ada dalam kontena atau se lainnya, dan bagasi dan barang
penumpang;

"kargo pindah kapal" ertinya mana-mana barang yang diimport yang dikonsain
melalui bil muatan terus dari  suatu tempat di luar Pelabuhan ke suatu tempat yang lain
di luar Pelabuhan—

(a) yang dipunggah atau yang akan dipunggah dari  kapal yang barang itu
diimport; dan

(b) sama ada dikembalikan ke kapal yang sama  atau dipindahkan ke kapal
yang akan membawanya sebelum dieksport,

sama ada barang itu  dipindahkan atau akan dipindahkan secara terus antara kapal
tersebut atau sama ada barang itu didaratkan di Pelabuhan selepas pengimportan dan
penyimpannya, menunggu untuk dieksport;

"kargo yang dipaletkan" ertinya kargo dalam bungkusan atau unit kecil yang
telah dibalut, diikat, atau dibalut dan diikat bersama dan ditempatkan di atas satu palet;

"kargo yang diunitkan" ertinya kargo dalam bungkusan atau unit kecil yang telah
dibalut, diikat, atau dibalut dan diikat bersama sebagai satu unit;

"KMK" ertinya Kontena Muatan Kurang yang diisytiharkan oleh syarikat
perkapalan atau ejennya dalam manifes, senarai pemunggahan kontena,  senara i
muatan atau penyata terdahulu eksport yang dikemukakan kepada Lembaga sebelum
pemunggahan atau pemuatan kargo ke atas kapal;

"KMP" ertinya Kontena Muatan Penuh yang diisytiharkan oleh syarikat
perkapalan atau ejennya dalam manifes, senarai pemunggahan kontena, senarai muatan
atau penyata terdahulu eksport yang dikemukakan kepada Lembaga sebelum
pemunggahan atau pemuatan kargo ke atas kapal;

"Kod BBMA" ertinya Kod Barang Berbahaya Maritim Antarabangsa yang
disiarkan oleh PMA yang dipinda dari semasa ke semasa;

"kontena DLU" ertinya kontena bersaiz standard ISO yang di  luar ukuran kerana
membawa apa-apa kargo yang bersaiz melebihi dimensi kontena itu;

"kumpulan" ertinya suatu komposisi tenaga kerja yang terdiri daripada
sebilangan pekerja;

 "Lembaga" ertinya Lembaga Pelabuhan Kelang;

"Operator Berlesen" ertinya operator pelabuhan yang di lesenkan di  bawah
seksyen 9 Akta Pelabuhan (Penswastaan) 1990 [Akta 422];

"palet" ertinya suatu peranti yang baginya suatu kuantiti kargo boleh
dihimpunkan untuk dija dikan satu unit muatan bagi maksud penghantaran kargo itu
atau pengendalian dan penyusunan kargo itu dengan bantuan perkakas mekanikal;

"pegawai pelabuhan" mempunyai erti yang diberikan kepadanya dalam Ordinan
Perkapalan Saudagar 1952 [Ord. 70/1952];

"Pelabuhan" ertinya Pelabuhan Klang di dalam had kawasan yang diisytihar kan
di bawah seksyen 6 Ordinan Perkapalan Saudagar 1952;

"Pengurus Besar" ertinya Pengurus Besar Lembaga;

"Pengurus Trafik" ertinya mana-mana pegawai yang dilantik oleh Lembaga at au
Operator Berlesen untuk menye lia atau men jaga operasi terminal, pembantunya dan
mana-mana pegawai yang bertindak di bawah atau dengan kuasanya;

"Pihak Berkuasa Zon Bebas" ertinya Lembaga Pelabuhan Kelang yang dilantik
di bawah subseksyen 3(2) Akta Zon Bebas 1990 [Akta 438];

"PK" ertinya panjang keseluruhan sesuatu kapal yang diukur dari titik paling
hadapan kapal itu ke titik paling belakang kapal itu;

"PMA" ertinya Pertubuhan Maritim Antarabangsa;

"premis pelabuhan" termasuklah mana-mana te mpat yang dimiliki atau
diduduki oleh Lembaga dan diuntukkan olehnya bagi pendaratan dan pengapalan apa -
apa kargo, termasuk mana -mana bahagian tebing sungai yang dimiliki atau diduduki
sedemikian yang telah diperbaiki untuk memudahkan pendaratan dan pengap alan itu
dan mana-mana persisir depan yang dimiliki atau diduduki sedemikian dan digunakan
bagi maksud  sedemikian;

 "SBK" ertinya Stesen Barangan Kontena di dalam premis pelabuhan;

"simpan tunggu" berhubung dengan suatu kapal, ertinya tidak digunakan sec ara
aktif dengan syarat bahawa nakhoda atau pemilik kapal itu telah memberi kan notis
bertulis kepada Lembaga dan pegawai pelabuhan bahawa kapal itu adalah dalam
keadaan sedemikian, dan Lembaga dan pegawai pelabuhan itu telah memberikan
kelulusan bertulis mereka;

"syif" ertinya tiga waktu bekerja yang b erulang-ulang dalam satu hari yang
ditentukan oleh Operator Berlesen;

"tan" ertinya satu tan metrik merangkumi satu ribu  kilogram atau satu meter
padu;

 "Tarikh Rasmi Pemunggahan" ertinya tarikh yang sesuat u kapal menyelesaikan
pemunggahannya;

 "Tempat Berlabuh" ertinya mana -mana tempat be rlabuh yang diluluskan oleh
Lembaga;

"TK" ertinya tanan kasar sesuatu kapal yang diukur mengikut Konvesyen
Antarabangsa Pengiraan Tanan Kapal 1969;

"transaksi" termasuklah semua perkhidmatan yang diberikan, dibekalkan atau
disediakan oleh Lembaga atau penggunaan kemudahan Lembaga oleh pengguna
pelabuhan.

BAHAGIAN II
CAJ AKAUN KAPAL

Jenis caj
3. Lembaga boleh mengenakan jenis caj yang berikut ke atas pengguna pelabuhan
dan caj itu hendaklah dikreditkan ke dalam akaun kapal:

(a) dius pelabuhan;

(b) caj marin disatukan;

(c) caj perkhidmatan permaliman;

(d) caj bagi p ermintaan lewat, perubahan atau pembatalan perkhidmatan
permaliman;

(e) caj penahanan malim;

(f) caj perkhidmatan bot tunda;

(g) caj bagi permintaan lewat, perubahan atau pembatalan perkhidmatan bot
tunda;

(h) caj penahanan bot tunda;

(i) caj dermaga;

(j) caj pemunggahan kargo;

(k) caj bagi permintaa n lewat, perubahan atau pembatalan perkhidmatan
pemunggahan kargo, dsb.;

(l) caj pengendalian dermaga bagi pindah kapal kargo am;

(m) caj pengendalian dermaga bagi pindah kapal pukal cecair;

(n) caj pengendalian dermaga bagi pindah kapal ro-ro;

(o) caj penumpang dan bagasi; dan

(p)  dius simpan tunggu.

Dius pelabuhan
4. (1) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan, berhubung dengan kapal yang memasuki
Pelabuhan, hendaklah membayar dius pelabuhan kepada Lembaga seperti yang berikut:

(a) dalam hal sesuatu kapal—

(i) yang memuatkan atau memunggah kargo atau mengambil
atau menurunkan penumpang; atau

(ii) yang singgah di Pelabuhan bagi apa -apa maksud lain selain
perenggan (b),

pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual A Baha gian 1 Jadual
Pertama; dan

(b) dalam hal sesuatu kapal yang singgah  di Pelabuhan bagi
mendapatkan bekalan minyak , mengambil bekalan air, mengambil
bekalan kapal atau membaiki kerosakan—

(i) bagi tempoh kurang dari pada dua ratus empat puluh  jam,
pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual B Bahagian 1
Jadual Pertama; dan

(ii) bagi tempoh lebih daripada dua ratus empat puluh  jam,
pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual A Bahagian  1
Jadual Pertama.

(2) Walau apa pun perenggan (1), semua kapal kepunyaan Kerajaan Malaysia
dan kapal yang singgah di Pelabuhan bagi maksud  kecemasan dikecualikan daripada
membayar dius pelabuhan.

Caj marin disatukan
 5. (1) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan, berhubung dengan kapal yang tiba di dan
berlepas dari Pelabuhan, hendaklah membayar caj marin disatukan kepada Lembaga
bagi perkhidmatan-perkhidmatan yang berikut:

(a) perkhidmatan permaliman dari tempat naik malim ke dermaga;

(b) perkhidmatan permaliman dari dermaga ke tempat naik malim;
              dan

(c) perkhidmatan bot tunda semasa menghimpit dan meninggalkan
himpitan.

 (2)  Caj marin disatukan dalam perenggan (1) hendaklah berdasarkan kepada
PK kapal bagi setiap persinggahan termasuk kapal p erang pada kadar yang dinyatakan
dalam Bahagian 2 Jadual Pertama.

Caj perkhidmatan permaliman
6. (1) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan, yang meminta perkhidmatan
permaliman selain perkhidmatan pe rmaliman yang di berikan di bawah
subperenggan 5(1)(a) dan (b) bagi pergerakan di dalam daerah permaliman, hendaklah
membayar caj perkhidmatan permaliman kepada Lembaga pada kadar yang dinyatakan
dalam Jadual A Bahagian 3 Jadual Pertama.

(2) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan , yang me minta perkhidmatan
permaliman bagi kapal yang mempunyai kerosakan  pendorongan atau ciri -ciri luar
biasa yang lain , hendaklah membayar caj perkhidmatan pe rmaliman kepada Lembaga
pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual B Bahagian 3 Jadual Pertama.

Caj bagi permintaan lewat, p erubahan atau pem batalan perkhidmatan
permaliman
7.  (1) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan hend aklah membuat permintaan,
perubahan atau pembatalan bagi perkhidmatan permaliman kepada Lembaga—

(a) tidak kurang daripada dua jam sebelum ketibaan kapal; atau

(b) tidak kurang dari pada satu jam sebelum perlepasan atau
penganjakan kapal di dalam daerah permaliman.

   (2)  Jika permintaan , perubahan atau pembatalan perkhidmatan pe rmaliman
dibuat kurang dari tempoh yang dinyatakan dalam perenggan (1), pengguna pelabuhan
hendaklah membayar ca j bagi permintaan  lewat, perubahan atau pembatalan kepada
Lembaga pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Bahagian 4 Jadual Pertama.

Caj penahanan malim
8. (1) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan  hendaklah membayar caj penahanan
malim kepada Lembaga jika—

(a) malim  menunggu  di  tempat  naik  malim   bagi   ketibaan  sesuatu
kapal;

  (b) malim menunggu di dermaga bagi penganjakan atau perlepasan
 sesuatu kapal; atau

  (c) malim men unggu di atas sesuatu kapal di tempat b erlabuh bagi
ketibaan, penganjakan atau perlepasan kapal.

 (2)  Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan hendaklah membayar caj penahanan
malim bagi setiap setengah jam atau sebahagian daripadanya yang dikira dari masa
perkhidmatan itu di minta pada kadar  yang dinyatakan dalam Bahagian 5 Jadual
Pertama.

Caj perkhidmatan bot tunda
9. (1) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan, yang mem inta perkhidmatan bot tunda
selain perkhidmatan bot tunda yang diperuntukkan di bawah subperenggan 5(1)(c)
bagi membantu, menganjak, menghimpit dan meninggalkan himpitan  di dalam daerah
permaliman, hendaklah membayar caj perkhidmatan bot tunda kepada Lembaga pada
kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual A Bahagian 6 Jadual Pertama.

(2) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan , yang meminta perkhidmatan bot tunda
bagi kapal yang mempunyai kerosakan pendorongan ata u ciri-ciri luar biasa yang lain,
hendaklah membayar caj perkhidmatan bot tunda kepada Lembaga pada kadar yang
dinyatakan dalam Jadual B Bahagian 6 Jadual Pertama.

(3) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan , yang meminta perkhidmatan pengiring
bot tunda bagi kapal yang mempunyai kerosakan pendorongan atau ciri -ciri luar biasa

yang lain, hendaklah membayar caj perkhidmatan pengiring bot tunda kepada Lembaga
pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual C Bahagian 6 Jadual Pertama.

Caj bagi permintaan lewat, perubahan atau pembatalan perkhidmatan bot tunda
10.  (1) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan hendaklah membuat per mintaan,
perubahan atau pembatalan bagi perkhidmatan bot tunda kepada Lembaga tidak
kurang daripada satu jam sebelum masa perkhidmatan itu dikehendaki.

(2)  Jika permintaan, perubahan atau pembatalan perkhidmatan bot tunda itu
dibuat kurang dari tempoh yang dinyatakan dalam perenggan (1),  pengguna pelabuhan
hendaklah membayar caj bagi permintaan lewat, perubahan atau pembatalan kepada
Lembaga pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Bahagian 7 Jadual Pertama.

Caj penahanan bot tunda
11. (1)  Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan hendaklah membayar caj penahanan bot
tunda kepada Lembaga bagi penahanan bot tunda disebabkan oleh kelewatan ketibaan
atau perlepasan kapal yang dikira dari masa perkhidmatan itu diminta pada kadar yang
dinyatakan dalam Bahagian 8 Jadual Pertama.

(2) Kelewatan ketibaan atau pe rlepasan kapal di bawah perenggan (1)
hendaklah disebabkan  oleh—

(a) kargo, pemiliknya atau ejennya;

(b) kapal, pemiliknya atau ejennya; atau

(c) apa-apa sebab  lain di luar kawalan  Lembaga atau Operator
Berlesen.

Caj  dermaga
12. (1) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan hendaklah membayar caj dermaga
kepada Lembaga seperti yang berikut:

(a)  dalam hal kapal kargo yang memuatkan atau memunggah  di
dermaga Lembaga atau Tempat Berlabuh, pada kadar yang
dinyatakan dalam Jadual A Bahagian 9 Jadual Pertama;

(b) dalam hal kapal penumpang yang berhimpit di dermaga Lembaga,
pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual B Bahagian 9 Jadual
Pertama; dan

(c)  dalam hal kapal perang asing yang berhimpit di dermaga Lembaga,
pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual C Bahagian 9 Jadual
Pertama.

(2)  Jika caj dermaga di bawah subperenggan (1)(a) atau (b) kurang daripada
satu ratus ringgit , caj dermaga minimum hendaklah te rpakai pada kadar yang
dinyatakan dalam Jadual D Bahagian 9 Jadual Pertama.

(3)  Suatu kapal kargo atau kapal penumpang yang melebihi satu ribu TK yang
menduduki dermaga bagi suatu tempoh tidak melebihi lapan jam atau enam jam
hendaklah diberikan pengurangan sebanyak dua puluh lima  peratus dan tiga puluh tiga
satu per tiga peratus masing-masingnya atas caj dermaga minimum yang disebut dalam
perenggan (2).

(4)  Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan, yang singgah lebih tempoh di dermaga
dan tidak mematuhi suatu noti s secara bertulis oleh Pengurus Trafik untuk
meninggalkan dermaga, hendaklah membayar caj dermaga kepada Lembaga pada kadar
yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual E Bahagian 9 Jadual Pertama.

Caj pemunggahan kargo
13.   Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan hendaklah memba yar caj pemunggahan kargo
kepada Lembaga berhubung dengan apa -apa import, eksport atau pindah kapal kargo
am atau ro-ro seperti yang berikut:

(a) dalam hal pemunggah kargo yang memuatkan atau memunggah kargo ke
dalam atau dari kapal, pada kadar yang dinya takan dalam Jadual A
Bahagian 10 Jadual Pertama;

(b)  dalam hal pemunggah kargo yang terlibat bagi operasi yang berikut, pada
kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual B Bahagian 10 Jadual Pertama:

(i) mengalihkan kargo ke atas kapal; atau

(ii) mendaratkan ka rgo di  dermaga dan kemudiannya mengapalkan
semula ke dalam kapal yang sama; dan

(c)  jika pemunggah kargo tambahan diperlukan, pada kadar yang dinyatakan
dalam Jadual C Bahagian 10 Jadual Pertama.

Caj bagi permintaan  lewat, perubaha n atau pembatalan perkhidmatan
pemunggahan kargo, dsb.
14. (1)  Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan hendaklah membuat  permintaan,
perubahan atau pembatalan bagi perkhidmatan pemunggahan kargo kepada Lembaga
tidak kurang daripada empat jam sebelum bermulanya tiap-tiap syif.

(2)  Jika permintaan , perubahan atau pembatalan perkhidmatan
pemunggahan kargo itu dibuat kurang dari tempoh yang dinyatakan dalam
perenggan (1), pengguna pe labuhan hendaklah membayar caj bagi permintaan lewat,
perubahan atau pembatalan kepada Lembaga pada k adar  yang dinyatakan dalam
Jadual A Bahagian 11 Jadual Pertama.

(3) Walau apa pun perenggan (2), caj bagi permintaan lewat, perubahan atau
pembatalan boleh diketepikan atas permohonan oleh pengguna pelabuhan kepada
Pengurus Trafik yang hendaklah mencadan gkan p enepian itu atau se lainnya kepada
Pengurus Besar yang keputusannya adalah muktamad.

(4) Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan hendaklah membayar caj pemunggahan
kargo kepada Lembaga bagi pemunggah kargo yang ditempah tetapi tidak bekerja,
melainkan disebabka n oleh hujan atau perkara yang timbul daripada kesalahan
Operator B erlesen pada kadar yang dinyatakan dalam Jadual B Bahagian 11 Jadual
Pertama.

Caj pengendalian dermaga bagi pindah kapal kargo am
15. Seseorang pengguna pelabuhan hendaklah membayar caj p engendalian dermaga
bagi pindah kapal kargo am kepada Lembaga berhubung dengan konsainan yang—

(a) dipunggah dari kapal ke dermaga Lembaga dan berada dalam jagaan
Operator Berlesen;

(b) bertanda pelabuhan bagi pelabuhan destinasi yang konsainan itu akan
dihantar;

(c) bertanda pelabuhan dalam manifes terus yang diberikan kepada Operator
Berlesen; dan

(d) dikapalkan oleh Operator Ber lesen ke dalam kapal yang akan
membawanya,

PORT AUTHORITIES ACT 1963

PORT KELANG AUTHORITY (SCALE OF RATES, DUES AND CHARGES) BY-LAWS 2012

IN exercise of the powers conferred by section s 16 and 29 of the Port Authorities Act
1963 [Act 488], the Port Kelang Authority, with the appro val of the Minister, makes the
following by-laws:

PART I
PRELIMINARY

Citation and commencement
1. (1) These by -laws may be cited as the Port Kelang Authority (Scale of
Rates, Dues and Charges) By-laws 2012.

(2) These By-laws come into operation on 1 July 2012.

Interpretation
In these By-laws, unless the context otherwise requires—

"Anchorage" means any anchorage approved by the Authority;

"Authority" means the Port Kelang Authority;

"Authority's wharf"  means a wharf  owned, controlled or operated by the
Authority;

"cargo" shall include livestock, minerals, wares and merchandise of every
description whether containerized or otherwise, and passenger luggage and effects;

"CFS" means the Container Freight Station within the port premises;

"Common Landing Date" means the date on which a ship completes its discharge;

"dangerous g oods" means dangerous goods whether in packaged form,
containerized or carried in bulk, and includes the goods classified by the Authority into
groups as specified in the Kela ng Port Authority By -laws 1965 [ L.N. 127/1965 ] and in
conformity with the IMDG Code and other relevant IMO publications as amended from
time to time and as adopted by the Authority;

"day" in relation to a transaction, means the period of twenty -four hours  from
the time of the commencement of the transaction;

"domestic trade ship" means any ship registered in Malaysia which is engaged in
domestic trade only;

"FCL" means Full Container Load as declared by the shipping line or its agent in
the manifest, con tainer discharge list, load list or export pre -advice submitted to the
Authority prior to the discharge or loading of cargo onto a ship;

"foreign going ship" means a ship other than a domestic trade ship;

"Free Zone Authority"  means the Port Kelang Auth ority appointed under
subsection 3(2) of the Free Zones Act 1990 [Act 438];

"gang" means a composition of labour comprising of a number of workers;

"General Manager" means General Manager of the Authority;

"GT" means the gross tonnage of a ship measured in accordance with the
International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships 1969;

"IMDG Code"  means the International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code
published by the IMO as amended from time to time;

"IMO" means the International Maritime Organisation;

"lay-up" in relation to a ship , means  not actively employed provided that the
master or owner of such ship has given written notice to the Authority and the port
officer that the ship is in such condition, and the Authority and the port officer have
given their written approval;

"LCL" means Less Container Load as declared by the shipping line or its agent in
the manifest, container discharge list, load list or export pre -advice submitted to the
Authority prior to the discharge or loading of cargo onto a ship;

"LOA" means the length overall of a ship measured from the extreme point
forward of the ship to the extreme point aft of the ship;

"Licensed Operator" means a port operator licensed under section 9 of the
Ports (Privatisation) Act 1990 [Act 422];

"OOG container" means an ISO standard size container which is out of gauge due
to the carrying of any cargo of the size exceeding the dimension of the container;

"package" includes any box, basket, barrel, case , receptacle, sack, bag, wrapper,
envelope or other covering or thing in which any cargo is placed for the purpose of
carriage, consignment, freight, importation or exportation;

"pallet" means a device of which a quantity of cargo can be assembled  to form a
unit load for the purpose of transporting the cargo or of handling and stacking the cargo
with the assistance of mechanical appliances;

"palletized cargo"  means the cargo in small packages or units which have been
wrapped, strapped, or wrapped and  strapped together and placed on a pallet;

"pilotage district" means an area declared by the Authority under section 29A of
the Port Authorities Act 1963;

"Port" means the Port Klang  within the limits declared under section 6 of the
Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952 [Ord. 70/1952];

"port officer" has the meaning assigned to it in the Merchant Shipping Ordinance
1952;

"port premises"  includes any place owned or occupied by the Authority and
appropriated by it for the landing and shipping of any cargo, including any portion of
the bank of the r iver so owned or occupied which has been improved to facilitate  such
landing and shipping and any foreshore so owned or occupied and used for such
purpose;

"shift" means three recurring working periods in a day as determined by the
Licensed Operator;

"shut-out" in relation to a cargo or container, means not carried on the ship's
voyage intended for the cargo or container;

"tonne" means one metric tonne of one thousand kilograms or one cubic metre;

"Traffic Manager" means any officer appointed by the A uthority or the Licensed
Operator to oversee or in charge of terminal operation, his assistant and any officer
acting under or with his authority;

"transaction" includes all services rendered, supplied or provided by the
Authority or the use of Authority's facilities by the port user;

"transhipment cargo" means any imported article that is consigned on a through
bill of lading from a place outside the Port to another place outside the Port—

(a) that is removed or to be removed from the ship in which it was  imported;
and

(b) either returned to the same ship or transferred to on -carrying ship before
being exported,

whether it is or is to be transferred directly between such ships or whether it is to be
landed in the Port after its importation and stored, pending exportation;

"unitized cargo"  means the cargo in small packages or units which have been
wrapped, strapped or wrapped and strapped together as a single unit;

"wharf"  includes any wall and bui lding adjoining the foreshore, sea-bed or a
river-bed.

PART II
SHIP'S ACCOUNT CHARGES

Type of charges
3. The Authority may impose the following types of charges on the port user and
such charges shall be credited into the ship's account:

(a) port dues;
(b) consolidated marine charge;
(c) pilotage service charge;
(d)     charge for the late request, changes or cancellation of pilotage service;
(e)        pilot detention charge;
(f)  tugboat services charge;
(g)  charge for the late request, changes or cancellation of tugboat service;
(h)        tugboat detention charge;
(i)        wharfage charge;
(j)        stevedorage charge;
(k) charge for the late request, changes or cancellation of stevedorage service,
etc.;
(l)        wharf handling charge for transhipment of general cargo;
(m) wharf handling charge for transhipment of liquid bulk;

(n)        wharf handling charge for transhipment of ro-ro;
(o)     passenger and luggage charge; and
(p) lay-up dues.

Port dues
4. (1) A port user, in relation to a ship entering the Port, shall pay the port dues
to the Authority as follows:

(a) in the case of a ship—

(i) loading or disc harging cargo or embarking or disembarking
passengers; or

(ii) calling the Port for any other purpose  other than paragraph
(b),

at the rate as specified in Table A of Part 1 of the First Schedule; and

(b) in the case of a ship calling the Port for bunkering , taking w ater,
ship's supplies or repair—

(i) for duration of less than two hundred and forty hours, at the
rate as specified in Table B of Part 1 of the First Schedule; and

(ii)  for duration of more than two hundred and forty hours, at the
rate as specified in Table A of Part 1 of the First Schedule.

(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), all ships belonging to the Government of
Malaysia and ships which call at the Port for the purpose of emergency are exempted
from paying the port dues.

Consolidated marine charge
5. (1) A port user, in relation to a ship arriving at and departing from the Port,
shall pay the consolidated marine charge to the Authority for the following services:

(a) pilotage service from pilot boarding ground to wharf;

(b) pilotage service from wharf to pilot boarding ground; and

(c)   tugboat service during berthing and unberthing of ship.

(2) The consolidated marine charge in subparagraph (1) shall be based on the
LOA of a ship per call including war ship at the rate as specified in Part 2 of the First
Schedule.

Pilotage service charge
6. (1)  A port user, who requests for pilotage service other than the pilotage
service provided for under subparagraph s 5(1)(a) and (b) for movement within the
pilotage district, shall pay the pilotage servic e charge to the Authority at the rate as
specified in  Table A of Part 3 of the First Schedule.

 (2) A port user, who requests for the pilotage service for a ship with defective
propulsion or other unusual characteristic , shall pay the pilotage service ch arge to the
Authority at the rate as specified in Table B of Part 3 of the First Schedule.

Charge for the late request, changes or cancellation of pilotage service
7. (1)  A port user  shall make a request for, changes to or cancellation of the
pilotage service to the Authority—

(a) not less than two hours before the arrival of a ship; or

(b) not less than one  hour before the departure or shifting of a ship
within the pilotage district.

(2)  Where the request, changes or cancellation of the pilotage service is made
less than the period specified in paragraph (1) , the port user shall pay a charge for the
late request, changes or cancellation to the Authority at the rate as specified in Part 4 of
the First Schedule.

Pilot detention charge
8. (1)  A port user shall pay the pilot detention charge to the Authority if—

(a) the pilot waits at the pilot boarding ground for the arrival of a ship;

(b) the pilot waits at the wharf for shifting or departure of  a ship; or

(c) the pilot waits on board a ship at anchorage for arrival, shifting or
departure of a ship.

(2)  A port user shall pay t he pilot detention charge for every half an hour or
part thereof calculated from the time the service is requested at the rate as specified in
Part 5 of the First Schedule.

Tugboat service charge
9. (1) A port user, who requests for the tugboat service other than the tugboat
service provided for under subparagraph 5(1)(c) for assisting, shifting, berthing and
unberthing within the pilotage district, shall pay the t ugboat service charge to the
Authority at the rate as specified in Table A of Part 6 of the First Schedule.

(2) A port user, who requests for the t ugboat service for a ship with defective
propulsion or other unusual characteristic, shall pay the tugboat service charg e to the
Authority at the rate as specified in Table B of Part 6 of the First Schedule.

(3) A port user, who requests for the tugboat escort  service for a ship with
defective propulsion or other unusual characteristic, shall pay the tugboat escort service
charge to the Authority at the rate as specified in Table C of Part 6 of the First Schedule.

Charge for the late request, changes or cancellation of tugboat service
10. (1)  A port user  shall make a request for, changes to or cancellation of the
tugboat service to the Authority not less than one hour before the time the service is
required.

(2)  Where the request, changes or cancellation of the tugboat service is made
less than the period specified in paragraph (1) , the port user shall pay a charge fo r the
late request, changes or cancellation to the Authority at the rate as specified in Part 7 of
the First Schedule.

Tugboat detention charge
11. (1)  A port user shall pay the tugboat detention charge to the Authority for the
detention of a tugboat due  to the delay in arrival or departure of a ship calculated from
the time the service is requested at the rate as specified in Part 8 of the First Schedule.

(2)  The delay in arrival or departure of a ship unde r paragraph (1) shall be
due to—
(a)   the cargo, its owner or agent;

(b)  the ship, its owner or agent; or

(c)  any other causes beyond the control of the Authority or Licensed
Operator.

Wharfage charge
 12. (1) A port user shall pay the wharfage charge to the Authority as follows:

(a) in the case of a cargo ship loading or discharging at the Authority's
wharf or Anchorage, at the rate as specified in Table A of Part 9 of
the First Schedule;

(b) in the case of a passenger ship berthed at the Authority's wharf, at
the rate as specified in Table B of Part 9 of the First Schedule; and

(c) in the case of foreign war ship berthed at the Authority's wharf, at
the rate as specified in Table C of Part 9 of the First Schedule.

(2) Where the wharfage charge  under subparagraph (1)(a) or (b) is less than
one hundred ringgit, the  minimum wharfage charge shall apply at the rate as specified
in    Table D of Part 9 of the First Schedule.

(3)  A cargo ship or  passenger ship  exceeding one thousand GT occupying the
wharf for a period not exceeding eight hours or s ix hours shall be given a reduction of
twenty-five per cent and thirty -three and one third per  cent respectively on the
minimum wharfage charge referred to in paragraph (2).

(4) A port user, who overstays at the wharf and fails to comply with a notice
in writing by the Traffic Manager to leave the wharf, shall pay the wharfage charge to
the Authority at the rate as specified Table E of Part 9 of the First Schedule.

Stevedorage charge
13.  A port user shall pay the stevedorage charge to the Authority in relation to any
import, export  or transhipment of general or ro-ro cargo as follows:

(a) in the case of stevedores  loading or discharging the cargo onto or from a
ship, at the rate as specified in Table A of Part 10 of the First Schedule;

(b) in the case of stevedores engaged for the following operations, at the rate
as specified in Table B of Part 10 of the First Schedule:

(i) shifting of cargo on board; or

(ii) landing cargo on the wharf and subsequently reshipping into the
same ship; and

(c) where additional stevedores are required, at the rate as specified in  Table
C of Part 10 of the First Schedule.

Charge for the late request, changes or cancellation of stevedorage service, etc.
14. (1)  A port user  shall make a request for, changes to or cancellation of the
stevedorage service to the Authority not less than four hours before the beginning of
each shift.

(2)  Where the request, changes or cancellation of stevedorage service is
made less than the period specified in paragraph (1), the port user shall pay a charge for
the late request, changes or cancellation to the Authority at the rate as specified in Table
A of Part 11 of the First Schedule.

(3)  Notwithstanding paragraph (2), the charge for the late request, changes
or cancellation may be waived on appl ication by the port user to the Traffic Manager
who shall recommend such waiver or otherwise to the General Manager whose decision
shall be final.

(4)  A port user shall pay the stevedorage charge to the Authority for
stevedores ordered but not worked, un less due to rain or matters arising from the fault
of the Licensed Operator at the rate as specified in Table B of Part 11 of the First
Schedule.

Wharf handling charge for transhipment of general cargo
15. A port user shall pay the w harf handling charge  for transhipment of general
cargo to the Authority in relation to consignments—

(a) discharged from ships onto the  Authority's whar f and remain in the
custody of the Licensed Operator;

(b) port-marked for the destination port to which the  consignments are to be
transported;

(c ) port-marked in the through manifest handed to the Licensed Operator;
and

(d) shipped by the Licensed Operator per the on-carrying ship,

at the rate as specified in Part 12 of the First Schedule.

Wharf handling charge for transhipment of liquid bulk
16. A port user shall pay the w harf handling charge  for transhipment of liquid bulk
to the Authority in relation to consignments—

(a) discharged from ships at the Authority's wharf  through pipelines into
private installation tank s and remain in the custody of the private
installation operator;

(b) port-marked in the through manifest handed to the Licensed Operator;
and

(c) shipped by the private installation operator per the on-carrying ship,

at the rate as specified in Part 13 of the First Schedule.

Wharf handling charge for transhipment of ro-ro
17. A port user shall pay the w harf handling charge for transhipment of ro-ro to the
Authority in relation to consignments—

(a) discharged from ships onto the Authority's whar f and remain in the
custody of the Licensed Operator;

(b) port-marked for the destination port to which the consignments  to be
transported;

(c ) port-marked in the through manifest handed to the Licensed Operator;
and

(d) shipped by the Licensed Operator per the on-carrying ship,

at the rate as specified in Part 14 of the First Schedule.

Passenger and luggage charge
18. A passenger, including a passenger in transit, shall pay the passenger and
luggage charge to the Authority for embarking or disembarking a s hip at the Authority's
wharf at the rate as specified in Part 15 of the First Schedule.

Lay-up dues
19. A port user shall pay the lay -up dues to the Authority for a ship on lay -up at the
Anchorage at the rate as specified in Part 16 of the First Schedule.

PART  III
SHIPPER OR CONSIGNEE'S ACCOUNT CHARGE

Type of charges
20. The Authority may impose the following types of charges on the port user and
such charges shall be credited into the shipper or consignee's account:

(a)  general wharf handling charge;
(b)        heavy lift wharf handling charge;
(c)        lifting service charge;
(d)        storage charge; and
(e)        overstaying charge.

General wharf handling charge
21.  A port user shall pay the general wharf handling charge to the Authority for—

(a) the receivi ng or  delivering break bulk cargo directly on the Authority's
wharf;

(b) the transfer ing of break bulk cargo from the Authority's wharf to a
warehouse or an open yard for storing and delivering to a consignee;

(c) the receiving of break bulk cargo from a shipper into the warehouse or an
open yard for storing and transferring such cargo to the Authority's wharf
for loading onto a  ship;

(d) the loading of cargo onto or discharging from a ship moored alongside
another ship berthed at the Authority's wharf or a ship at the Anchorage;

(e) the handling of liquid bulk cargo through a port user's pipeline including
the use of crane for handling the pipeline;

(f) the handling of ro-ro cargo, in the case of—

(i) import cargo, the transfer of import cargo from the  Authority's
wharf to an open yard for storing and delivering to a consignee; or

(ii) export cargo, the receiving of export cargo from the shipper into an
open yard for storing and transferring such cargo to the Authority's
wharf for loading onto a ship; or

(g) the receiving or delivering of dry  bulk cargo directly on the Authority's
wharf,

at the rate as specified in Part 1 of the Second Schedule.

Heavy lift wharf handling charge
22. (1)  A port user shall pay the heavy lift wharf handling charge to the Authority
in relation to any package or article weighing more than one tonne for—

(a) receiving  or delivering directly on the Authority's wharf;

(b) transferring from the Authority's wharf to a warehouse or open
yard for storing and delivering to a consignee; or

(c) receiving at the warehouse or open yard for storing and
transferring to the Authority's wharf for loading onto a ship,

at the rate as specified in Part 2 of the Second Schedule.

 (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a port user shall be exempt ed from
paying the heavy lift wharf handling charge for any p ackage or article weighing not
more than three tonne in deadweight which are amenable to forklift operations either
through palletization or skids, as may be determined by the Traffic  Manager, in respect
of import and export cargo.

(3) Where the port user is exempted from paying the heavy lift wharf
handling charge under paragraph (2), the port user shall pay the general wharf handling
charge at the rate as specified in item 1, 2, 3 or 4 of Part 1 of the Second Schedule.

Lifting service charge
23.  (1) A port user shall pay the lifting service charge to the Authority for a single
heavy lift or non-palletized cargo in the warehouse or open yard at the rate as  specified
in Part 3 of the Second Schedule.

(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1) , a port user shall be exempted from
paying the lifting service charge for any package or article weighing not more than three
tonne in deadweight which is amenable to forklift operations either through
palletization or skids, as may be determined by the Traffic Manager.

Storage charge
24.  (1)  A port user shall pay the storage charge to the Authority for storing—

(a) import cargo in the warehouse or open yard at the rate as specified
in Table A of Part 4 of the Second Schedule;

(b) export or shut-out cargo in the warehouse or open yard at the rate
as specified in Table B of Part 4 of the Second Schedule;

(c) transhipment or over landed cargo in the warehouse or open yard
at the rate as specified in Table C of Part 4 of the Second Schedule;

(d) permitted import dangerous goods Groups II and III in the
warehouse or open yard at the rate as specified in Table D of Part 4
of the Second Schedule;

(e) permitted export dangerous goods Groups II and III in the
warehouse or open yard at the rate as specified in Table E of Part 4
of the Second Schedule;

(f) damaged cargo in the warehouse or open yard commencing from
the time of receipt of such cargo at the rate as specified in Table A,
B, C, D or E of Part 4 of the Second Schedule ;

(g) import and transhipment ro -ro cargo in the open yard at the rate
as specified in Table F of Part 4 of the Second Schedule; or

(h) export ro-ro cargo in the open yard at the rate as specified in Table
G of Part 4 of the Second Schedule.

 (2)  The import cargo referred to in subparagraph (1) (a) shall be entitled to
a free storage period of three days commencing from the Common Landing Date of the
ship, and the storage charge shall be calculated after the expiry of such free  storage
period until the cargo is collected by the consignee.

(3)  The export or  shut-out cargo referred to in subparagraph (1) (b) shall be
entitled to a free storage period of seven days commencing from the end of the shift
during which the cargo are re ceived into the warehouse or open yard, and the storage
charge shall be calculated after the expiry of such free storage period until the actual
time of berthing of the ship on which the cargo are to be loaded.

(4)  The transhipment or over landed cargo referred to in subparagraph (1)(c)
shall be entitled to a free storage period of twenty -eight days commencing from the
Common Landing  Date of the first ship, and the storage charge shall be calculated after
the expiry of such free storage period until the actual time of berthing of the second ship
on which the cargo is to be loaded.

(5) The import dangerous goods referred to in subparagraph (1) (d) shall not
be entitled to any free storage period.

(6) The export dangerous goods referred to in subparagraph ( 1)(e) shall be
entitled to a free storage period of three days commencing from the end of the shift
during which the cargo is received into the warehouse, and the storage charge shall be
calculated after the expiry of such free storage period until the actual time of berthing of
the ship on which the cargo is to be loaded.

(7)  The import ro -ro cargo referred to in subparagraph (1) (g) shall be
entitled to a free storage period of three days commencing from the Common Landing
Date of the ship and if the ro-ro cargo is collected by the consignee after the free storage
period, the storage charge shall be calculated from the Common Landing Date.

(8) The export ro -ro cargo referred to in subparagraph (1) (h) shall be
entitled to a free storage period of seven d ays commencing from the end of the shift
during which the ro -ro cargo is received in the open yard, and the storage charge shall
be calculated after the expiry of such free storage period until the actual time of
berthing of the vessel on which the ro-ro cargo is to be loaded.

(9)   The transhipment ro-ro cargo referred to in subparagraph (1) (g) shall be
entitled to a free storage period of twenty -eight days commencing from the Common
Landing Date of the first ship.

(10)  Notwithstanding paragraph (9), t he transhipment ro -ro cargo which is
not transhipped within the free storage period shall be treated as import ro -ro cargo,
and the storage charge shall be re-calculated from the Common Landing Date of the first
ship until the actual time of berthing of th e on-carrying ship at the rate as specified in
Table F of     Part 4 of the Second Schedule.

(11)  Shut-out cargo which is not shipped but subsequently removed from the
port by the port user shall not entitled to any free storage period.

(12) The Authori ty may remove any cargo left without approval of the
Authority at any time and the cargo owner shall bear the cost of such removal.

Exemption of storage charge
25. A port user shall be exempted from paying the storage charge to the Authority in
the following circumstances:

(a) when any cargo is detained by the police, customs or other enforcement
agencies or under the court order, the period of exemption shall be
calculated from the date of detention or the date of filing delivery
instruction, whichever is the later, up to the date of release of such
detention provided that a declaration made by the port user in relation to
such cargo shall be in compliance with the requirements as determined
by the police, customs or other enforcement agencies;

(b) when any cargo is not traceable at the time the delivery was applied for in
respect of which a "NOT FOUND" remark was made on the document, the
period of exemption shall be calculated from the day following the date on
which the "NOT FOUND" remark was made up to t he date the cargo was
traced;

(c) when any cargo is shown as short landed in the outturn report of the ship
but subsequently the cargo was traced, the period of exemption shall be
calculated from the date the cargo was shown as short landed  to the date
the cargo was traced;

(d) when any cargo clearance is delayed due to misdelivery, the period of
exemption shall be calculated from the date following the date on which a
"NOT FOUND" remark was made up to  the date the cargo was traced; and

(e)        when any cargo which  in  the  opinion of the General Manager is intended
for  charitable  purposes  provided  that  an  exemption from  the  customs
duty by the importer is obtained.

Overstaying charge
26. A port user shall pay the overstaying charge to the Au thority for any import
cargo stored in the warehouse which is not removed within the period of three days
after the Common Landing Date at the rate as specified in Part 5 of the Second Schedule.

PART IV
SHIP, CONSIGNEE OR SHIPPER'S ACCOUNT CHARGES

Type of charges
27. The Authority may impose the following types of charges on the port user and
such charges shall be credited into the ship, consignee or shipper's account:

(a) handling charge for containers;
(b) handling charge for OOG containers;
(c) handling charge for heavy lift or uncontainerized cargo;
(d) shifting and re-stow charge for containers;
(e) opening and closing of hatch cover charge;
(f) extra movement charge for containers;
(g) reefer container service charge;
(h) storage charge for containers; and

(i) overstaying charge for containers.

Handling charge for containers
28. (1) A port user shall pay the handling charge for container s to the Authority
for the handling of containers using the Port's crane at the rate as specified in Part 1 of
the Third Schedule.

(2) The handl ing charge for containers under paragraph ( 1) is for the
following purposes:

(a) in the case of the handling of import FCL  containers containing
non-dangerous goods or empty containers for—

(i)  discharging the containers from a ship;

(ii)  moving the containers from a wharf to a container yard for
stacking;

(iii)  mounting the containers onto a haulier's trailer or railway
wagon for delivery; and

(iv) moving the empty containers from the ship to the container
yard for storage and subsequently removed to the CFS;

(b) in the case of the handling of export FCL containers containing
non-dangerous goods or empty containers for—

(i)  lifting the containers from a haulier's trailer or railway
wagon;

(ii)  stacking the containers at a container yard;

(iii) moving the containers to a wharf; and

(iv)  loading the containers onto a ship;

(c) in the case of the handling of import FCL containers containing
dangerous goods Groups I, II and III for—

(i)  discharging the containers from a ship;

(ii)  moving  the containers from the wharf to a container yard
for stacking, if storage in the Port is permitted;

(iii) mounting the contain ers onto a haulier's trailer for
delivery; and

(iv)   mounting the container s onto a haulier's trailer for direct
delivery, if storage in the Port is not permitted;

(d) in the case of the handling of export FCL containers containing
dangerous goods Groups I, II and III for—

(i)  lifting the containers from a haulier's trailer;

(ii)  stacking the containers at a contain er yard, if storage in the
Port is permitted;

(iii) moving the containers to  a wharf;

(iv) loading the  containers onto a ship; and

(v) loading the containers directly from a haulier's trailer onto
a ship, if storage in the Port is not permitted;

(e) in the case of the handling of import LCL containers containing
non-dangerous goods for—

(i)  discharging the containers from a ship;

(ii)  moving the containers from a wharf to a container yard for
stacking;

(iii)  mounting the containers onto a  trailer for transfer to the
CFS;

(iv)  the lift-on lift-off services at the CFS;

(v) unstuffing of the containers, storing and delivering the
cargo to the port user; and

(vi)  returning the empty containers to the container yard;

(f) in the case of the handling of export LCL  containers containing
non-dangerous goods for—

(i)  receiving break bulk cargo and storing  at the CFS;

(ii)  transferring the empty containers  from the container yard
to the CFS;

(iii)  stuffing the cargo into containers;

(iv)  transferring the  containers to a container yard;

(v)  stacking the containers at a container yard; and

(vi)  transferring the containers to a wharf for loading onto a
ship;

(g) in the case of the handling of inward transhipment FCL container s
or empty containers for—

(i)  discharging the transhipment containers from the first ship;
and

(ii)  moving the transhipment containers from a wharf to a
container yard; and

(h) in the case of the handling of outward transhipment FCL
containers  or empty containers for—

(i) moving the transhipment containers from a container yard
to wharf; and

(ii) loading the transhipment containers onto the on -carrying
ship.

 (3) The transhipment containers specified under subparagraph s 2(g) and (h)
shall be transhipped—

(a) in the case of FCL containers, within three hundred and thirty -six
hours; or

(b) in the case of FCL dangerous goods containers, within one hundred
and sixty-eight hours,

from the time of berthing of the first ship to the time of berthing of the on-carrying ship.

(4) Where t he transhipment containers are not transhipped within the
periods specified in paragraph (3), the transhipment containers shall be subject to
import containers charge which shall be re-calculated from the time of berthing of the
first ship at the rate as specified in items 1 and 2 of Part 1 of the Third Schedule.

Handling charge for OOG containers
29.  (1) A port user shall pay the handling charge for OOG containers  to the
Authority for the handling of OOG containers using the Port's  crane at the rate as
specified in Part 2 of the Third Schedule.

(2)  The handling charge for the OOG containers shall include the lifting of the
containers on or off from the ship and the port user shall arrange for his own chassis or
low loaders to deliver or receive the containers at the wharf side.

(3)  Where additional gears are required for the handling of the OOG
containers, the supply of the gears shall be charged separately to the port user.

(4)  Where the OOG containers are—

(a) to be delivered to the port user; or

(b) to be shipped on FCL basis,

or required to be unstuffed or stuffed,  a port user shall pay the handling charge for FCL
or LCL at the rate as specified in items 1, 2 and 3 of Part 1 of the Third Schedule in
addition to any charges payable under paragraphs (1) and (3).

Handling charge for heavy lift or uncontainerized cargo
30. (1) A port user shall pay the handling charge for heavy lift or uncontainerized
cargo to the Authority for the handling  of heavy lift or uncontaineri zed cargo using the
Port's crane at the rate as specified in Part 3 of the Third Schedule.

 (2) The handling charge for heavy lift or uncontaineri zed cargo shall include
the lifting of the heavy lift or uncontaineri zed cargo on or off from the ship  and the port
user shall arrange for his own chassis or low loader to deliver or receive the heavy lift
or uncontainerized cargo at the wharf side.

(3)  Where additional gears are required for the handling of the heavy lift or
uncontainerized cargo, the supply of the gears shall be charged separately to the port
user.

(4) Where the port user is unable to take direct delivery at the wharf, he shall
remove or cause to be removed the cargo from the port premises and the port user shall
bear the cost of such removal.

Shifting and re-stow charge for containers
31.  A port user shall pay the shifting and re-stow charge for containers on board ship
to the Authority for shifting of containers using t he Port's c rane for the following
purposes:

(a) for shifting of containers from one cell to another cell within the same bay
or hatch of a ship at the rate as specified in paragraph (a) of item 1 of Part
4 of the Third Schedule;

(b) for shifting of containers from one bay or hatch and reshipped to the next
bay or hatch of the sa me ship at the rate as specified in paragraph (b) of
item 1 of Part 4 of the Third Schedule; and

(c ) for landing of containers on the wharf and re-stowing the same containers
into the same bay or hatch, or into a different bay or hatch of the same
ship at the rate as specified in paragraph (c) of item 1 of Part 4 of the
Third Schedule.

Opening and closing of hatch cover charge
32.  A port user shall pay the opening and closing of hatch cover charge to the
Authority for the opening and closing of hatch cover on board ship using the Port's
crane at the rate as specified in Part 5 of the Third Schedule.

Extra movement charge for containers
33. A port user shall pay the extra movement charge for containers to the Authority
for the handling of containers i n the container yard at the rate  as specified in Part 6 of
the Third Schedule.

Reefer container service charge
34. A port user shall pay the reefer container service charge to the Authority for the
reefer container services provided at the rate as specif ied in Part 7 of  the Third
Schedule.

Storage charge for containers
35. (1) A port user shall pay the storage charge for containers to the Authority for
storing—

(a) import FCL or LCL containers at the rate as specified in Table A of
Part 8 of the Third Schedule;

(b) export FCL or LCL containers at the rate as specified in Table B of
Part 8 of the Third Schedule;

(c) import empty containers at the rate as specified in Table C of Part 8
of the Third Schedule;

(d) export empty containers and unstuffed FCL or LCL empty
containers at the rate as specified in Table D of Part 8 of the Third
Schedule;

(e) import FCL or LCL containers from any port in Malaysia at the rate
as specified in Table E of Part 8 of the Third Schedule;

(f) export FCL or LCL containers to any port in Malaysia  at the rate as
specified in Table F of Part 8 of the Third Schedule;

(g) import empty containers from any port in Malaysia at the rate as
specified in Table G of Part 8 of the Third Schedule;

(h) export empty containers to any port in Malaysia at the rate as
specified in Table H of Part 8 of the Third Schedule;

(i) import FCL or LCL dangerous goods containers at the rate as
specified in Table I of Part 8 of the Third Schedule;

(j) export FCL or LCL dangerous goods containers at the rate as
specified in Table J of Part 8 of the Third Schedule;

(k) chassis trailer with or without containers stored in the container
yard or any other area within the port premise at the rate as
specified in Table K of Part 8 of the Third Schedule;

(l) the break bulk cargo at the CFS  at the rat e as specified in Table A,
B or C of Part 4 of the Second Schedule; and

(m) the break bulk dangerous goods at the CFS at the rate as specified
in Table D or E of Part 4 of the Second Schedule.

(2) Import FCL or LCL containers or empty containers shall be ent itled to a
free storage period of seventy -two hours commencing from the time the containers are
received in the container yard after unloading from the ship, and the storage charge
shall be calculated after the expiry of such free storage period until the time of exit of
the containers from the container yard.

(3) Export FCL or LCL containers shall be entitled to a free storage period of
seventy-two hours commencing from the time of receipt of the containers at the
container yard, and the storage charge sh all be calculated after the expiry of such free

storage period until the time of exit of the containers from the container yard for
loading on board ship.

(4) Export empty containers and FCL or LCL containers which have been
unstuffed and are kept as empty containers in the container yard shall not be entitled to
any free storage period, and the storage charge shall be calculated from the time the
containers are stored in the container yard until the time of exit of the containers from
the container yard.

(5) Import FCL or LCL containers or empty containers from any port in
Malaysia shall be entitled to a free storage period of one hundred and sixty -eight hours
commencing from the time the containers are received in the container yard after
unloading from t he ship, and the storage charge shall be calculated after the expiry of
such free storage period until the time of exit of the containers from the container yard.

(6) Export FCL or LCL containers or empty containers to any port in Malaysia
shall be entitl ed to a free storage period of one hundred and sixty -eight hours
commencing from the time of receipt of the containers in the container yard, and the
storage charge shall be calculated after the expiry of such free storage period until the
time of exit of the containers from the container yard for loading on board ship.

(7)   Transhipment containers shall be entitled to a free storage period of three
hundred and thirty-six hours commencing from the time of berthing of the first ship.

(8) Notwithstanding p aragraph (7), the transhipment containers which are
not transhipped within the free storage period shall be subject to an import container
storage charge under subparagraph (1)(a) or (c) at the rate as specified in Table A or C
of Part 8 of the Third Schedule.

(9) Chassis trailers with or without containers stored in the container yard or
any designated area within the port premise shall be entitled to a free storage period of
seventy-two hours commencing from the time the chassis is received at the contai ner

yard or designated area, and the storage charge shall be calculated after the expiry of
such free storage period.

(10) Import FCL or LCL dangerous goods containers permitted for storage by
the Authority shall be entitled to a free storage period of se venty-two hours
commencing from the time the container is received in the container yard after
unloading from the ship, and the storage charge shall be calculated after the expiry of
such free storage period until the time of exit of the container from the container yard.

(11) Export FCL or LCL dangerous goods containers permitted for storage by
the Authority shall be entitled to a free storage period of seventy -two hours
commencing from the time of receipt of the containers at the container yard, and the
storage charge shall be calculated after the expiry of such free storage period until the
time of exit of the containers from the container yard for loading on board ship.

(12)    Transhipment dangerous goods containers permitted for storage by the
Authority shall be entitled to a free storage period of one hundred and sixty -eight hours
commencing from the time of berthing of the first ship.

(13) Notwithstanding paragraph (12), the transhipment dangerous goods
containers permitted for storage by the Auth ority which are not transhipped within the
free storage period shall be subject to an import container storage charge  under
subparagraph (1)(i) at the rate as specified in Table I of Part 8 of the Third Schedule.

(14) Cargo in the CFS shall be entitled to  a free storage period of seventy -two
hours commencing from the time the cargo is received at the CFS.

(15) Notwithstanding paragraph (14), the cargo in the CFS which are not
removed within the free storage period shall be subject to a storage charge ca lculated
from the time the cargo is received at the CFS.

Exemption of storage charge for containers
36. A port user shall be exempted from paying the s torage charge for containers to
the Authority in the following circumstances:

(a) when any container  is detained by the police, customs or other
enforcement agencies or under the court order, the pe riod of exemption
shall be calculated from the date of detention or the date of filing delivery
instruction, whichever is later, up to the date of release of such detention
provided that a declaration made by the port user in relation to such
cargo shall be in compliance with the requirements as determined by the
police, customs or other enforcement agencies;

(b) when any container is not traceable at the ti me the delivery was applied
for in respect of which a "NOT FOUND" remark was made, the period of
exemption shall be calculated from the day following the date on which
the "NOT FOUND " remark was  made up to the date the container was
traced;

(c) when any container clearance is delayed due to misdelivery, the period of
exemption shall be calculated from the date following the date on which
a "NOT FOUND " remark  was made up to  the date the container was
traced; and

(d) when cargo in FCL container wh ich in the opinion of the General Manager
is intended for charitable purposes provided that an exemption from the
customs duty by the importer is obtained.

Overstaying charge for containers
37. A port user shall pay the overstaying charge for containers to the Authority for
any import container stored in the container yard which is not removed within the free
storage period at the rate as specified in Part 9 of the Third Schedule.

PART V
MISCELLANEOUS

Determination of weight
38. The Authority shall determine the weight of goods for the purpose of calculating
charges by way of the following:

(a) weighing;

(b) requiring the consignor or consignee to furnish particulars of the weight;
or

(c) assessing the weight measurement or estimation.

Basis of charges
39. (1)  The Authority may impose charges on measurement tonnage if the weight
tonnage cannot be ascertained or vice versa.

 (2) The charges shall be based on weight or measurement tonnage,
whichever is greater.

(3)  In the case of bulk cargo,  the charges shall be based on tonnage declared
in the manifest tonnage or determined by draft survey.

(4) For the purpose of this by -law, one thousand kilograms is equivalent to
one tonne and one cubic metre is equivalent to one tonne.

Calculation of measurement and weight
40. (1) In calculating the measurement, fractions of a cubic metre shall be
rounded-up to the next higher cubic metre.

(2) In calculating the weight, fractions of a tonne shall be  rounded-up to the
next higher tonne.

Payment of charges
41. (1) Any payment of charges shall be payable by a ledger or other credit
account accompanied by a financial security.

(2)  Where credit facilities are made available by the Authority to a port user,
the outstanding amount shall be settled within the period of thirty days from the date of
the invoice.

(3) The outstanding amount which is not settled within the period as
specified in paragraph (2) shall be subject to a two per cent per month surcharge if it is
not settled within a period of thirty days.

(4) The outstanding amount referred to in paragraph (3) shall not include the
surcharge amount.

Undercharge
42. The Authority shall be entitled to collect any amount of charges which may be
ascertained to have been undercharged or that which may otherwise be found to be
due, and shall demand in writing the payment of any such amount within six years from
the date of transaction.

Time limit and condition for refund of overcharge
43. (1) A port user shall be entitled to a refund of any overcharge if a claim for
refund is submitted in writing to the Authority w ithin six years from the date of  the
transaction.

(2) A p ort user who claims for refund of any overcharge shall provide full
information supported by such other  documentary evidence as may be required by the
Authority.

(3) In the case of cargo, the Authority shall accept a claim for refund if the
port user has disputed the measurement or weight of such cargo at the time such cargo
was measured or weighed.

Liability for charges
44. (1) A consignee shall be liable for all charges on inward cargo.

(2) A shipper shall be liable for all charges on outward cargo.

(3) A master of a ship or ship's agent shall be responsible for all charges
recoverable from the ship and on transhipment cargo.

Application for work on ships
45. An a pplication for any labour requisition to work on ship for each of the shift
shall be made to the Traffic Manager at least four hours before the beginning of the shift.

Labour supply
46. (1) Where any ship berthed or anchored in  Port uses any wharf, pier, jetty or
anchorage belonging to or under the control of the Authority, the Authority or the
Licensed Operator may provide labour of every description in connection with the
loading or discharging of cargo and recover the charges as prescribed under these By -
laws.

(2) Where the Licensed Operator  does not provide labour  referred to in
paragraph (1), the Authority may authorize and approve by way of licens ing any person
to provide labour in connection with the loading or discharging of cargo.

Disposal of unclaimed goods
47. (1)   Cargo without disposal instructions will be stored subject to storage
charges prescribed under these By-laws and notice of arrival, if possible, shall be served
by the Authority upon the person appearing in the Bill of Lading  to be the consignee.

(2)  After any cargo including damaged cargo have been stored by the
Authority for a period of twenty-one days, the Authority may cause a notice to be served
to the consignee by way of registered post requiring him to remove the cargo within
seven days from the date of notice.

(3) Where the notice cannot be served to the consignee or the consignee fails
to comply with the notice  under paragraph (2) , the Authority may dispose of the ca rgo
by public auction of which three days notice shall be published in two local newspapers.

(4)  All charges due to the Authority in respect of such cargo including all
expenses of notice and sale shall be recovered by the Authority from the proceeds of the
sale, and the surplus, if any, shall be rendered to any person entitled thereto.

(5) Over landed cargo shall, on receipt of instructions from the ship's agents,
be stored by the Authority subject to storage charges.

(6) For the purpose of paragraph (5), paragraphs (2), (3) and (4) shall apply
except that such notice requiring removal of the cargo shall not be made until the cargo
has been stored for a period of fourty-two days.

(7) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1), (2), (3), (4), (5) and (6)—

(a)  any perishable cargo unclaimed  within twenty-four hours after
arrival shall be sold or otherwise disposed of by the Authority; and

(b)  any cargo such as firearms, ammunition and explosive without
approved permits or contraband shall be handed over to the police
or customs by the Auth ority for disposal in accordance with the
relevant laws.

Re-issuance of documents
48. If any voucher, tally sheet, invoice or other documents relating to the delivery of
cargo issued by the Licensed Operator  to the port user  has been lost or accidentally

defaced or the particulars have become illegible, the Licensed Operator upon being
satisfied as to such loss, defacement or illegibility shall, on payment of a fee of twenty-
five ringgit, re-issue a copy of the original document or a replacement document , as the
case may be.

General conditions
49. (1)  The Authority shall not provide any service or accommodation to any
person unless such person makes a request in writing for the same and where such a
request is made, the Authority may, where it deems f it or to do so in the interest of the
Authority, refuse the request without assigning any reason.

(2) The Authority shall not act on any delivery order for delivery of import
cargo unless such order in writing has been received from the port user.

(3) The Authority shall not act on any shipment order for the shipment of any
export cargo unless such order in writing has been received from the port user.

(4) A port user shall comply with the customs and the Free Zone Authority's
requirements before the delivery or shipment is carried out by the Licensed Operator.

(5) The Authority may, upon notification to the port user, remove the cargo at
any time as it considers necessary, and all cost incurred shall be payable by the port
user.

Foreshore charge
50. A consignee or shipper shall pay the foreshore charge for cargo, livestock and
vehicles passing over the foreshore within the Port limit other than the foreshore within
the port premises under the administration of Licensed Operator at the rate as specified
in Part 1 of the Fourth Schedule.

Revocation
51. The Kelang Port Authority (Scale of Rates, Dues and Charges) By -laws 1966
[P.U.  126/1966] are revoked.
